You improve how a model reads case records into facts for a procedure. Rules written from the procedure decide each case from those facts. The rules are fixed; only the reader's notes can change.

Below are the facts the reader fills in, the procedure, and cases where the decision came out as "review" (a fact the rules needed was left unknown) or disagreed with the answer a lawyer gave. For each case you see the record, the lawyer's answer, the decision, the facts the reader filled in, and the rules that might have applied.

Write notes for the reader: general guidance on how records in this domain are written and what they mean, so the reader fills in facts the way a careful lawyer would read the same record. For example, what an opening sentence settles, what a record's silence about a topic means, or how to read a stated price.

- Write rules of reading, not answers. Never name a case, a company in a case, or a case's outcome.
- Don't tell the reader to guess. Each note must say what in a record justifies a value, so a person auditing the reader could check it.
- Keep it under 300 words.

## The procedure

# Telemarketing Sales Rule: deceptive acts before and during a sale

16 CFR 310.3(a)(1) and (a)(2), with the definitions from 16 CFR 310.2 whose terms they use. The text is the eCFR's, amended to 2025-10-01, word for word; only the numbering is ours, so the rule format can cite it. Section 1 is ours: the regulation names no outcomes and doesn't say what an unknown fact means.

Numbering: 2 is 310.3(a) and (a)(1), and 2.1 to 2.8 are (a)(1)(i) to (viii). 3 is (a)(2), and 3.1 to 3.10 are (a)(2)(i) to (x). 4.1 onwards are definitions from 310.2: 4.1 is 310.2(e), 4.2 is 310.2(j), 4.3 is 310.2(k), 4.4 is 310.2(n), 4.5 is 310.2(o), 4.6 is 310.2(s), 4.7 is 310.2(t), 4.8 is 310.2(w), 4.9 is 310.2(y), 4.10 is 310.2(bb), 4.11 is 310.2(cc), 4.12 is 310.2(ee), 4.13 is 310.2(hh), 4.14 is 310.2(ii).

## 1. How a case is decided

This procedure applies the rule below to one telemarketing sale. Every case receives exactly one outcome:

- **Violation**: the conduct is a deceptive telemarketing act or practice and a violation of the rule.
- **Review**: a required fact has not been established yet. A reviewer finds it before deciding.
- **No violation**: nothing in sections 2 and 3 applies.

1.1. When more than one outcome applies, the most severe governs: Violation, then Review, then No violation.

1.2. A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be cleared as no violation.

## 2. Disclosures before the customer consents to pay

Prohibited deceptive telemarketing acts or practices. It is a deceptive telemarketing act or practice and a violation of this part for any seller or telemarketer to engage in the following conduct:

Before a customer consents to pay for goods or services offered, failing to disclose truthfully, in a clear and conspicuous manner, the following material information:

2.1. The total costs to purchase, receive, or use, and the quantity of, any goods or services that are the subject of the sales offer;

2.2. All material restrictions, limitations, or conditions to purchase, receive, or use the goods or services that are the subject of the sales offer;

2.3. If the seller has a policy of not making refunds, cancellations, exchanges, or repurchases, a statement informing the customer that this is the seller's policy; or, if the seller or telemarketer makes a representation about a refund, cancellation, exchange, or repurchase policy, a statement of all material terms and conditions of such policy;

2.4. In any prize promotion, the odds of being able to receive the prize, and, if the odds are not calculable in advance, the factors used in calculating the odds; that no purchase or payment is required to win a prize or to participate in a prize promotion and that any purchase or payment will not increase the person's chances of winning; and the no-purchase/no-payment method of participating in the prize promotion with either instructions on how to participate or an address or local or toll-free telephone number to which customers may write or call for information on how to participate;

2.5. All material costs or conditions to receive or redeem a prize that is the subject of the prize promotion;

2.6. In the sale of any goods or services represented to protect, insure, or otherwise limit a customer's liability in the event of unauthorized use of the customer's credit card, the limits on a cardholder's liability for unauthorized use of a credit card pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1643;

2.7. If the offer includes a negative option feature, all material terms and conditions of the negative option feature, including, but not limited to, the fact that the customer's account will be charged unless the customer takes an affirmative action to avoid the charge(s), the date(s) the charge(s) will be submitted for payment, and the specific steps the customer must take to avoid the charge(s); and

2.8. In the sale of any debt relief service: (A) the amount of time necessary to achieve the represented results, and to the extent that the service may include a settlement offer to any of the customer's creditors or debt collectors, the time by which the debt relief service provider will make a bona fide settlement offer to each of them; (B) to the extent that the service may include a settlement offer to any of the customer's creditors or debt collectors, the amount of money or the percentage of each outstanding debt that the customer must accumulate before the debt relief service provider will make a bona fide settlement offer to each of them; (C) to the extent that any aspect of the debt relief service relies upon or results in the customer's failure to make timely payments to creditors or debt collectors, that the use of the debt relief service will likely adversely affect the customer's creditworthiness, may result in the customer being subject to collections or sued by creditors or debt collectors, and may increase the amount of money the customer owes due to the accrual of fees and interest; and (D) to the extent that the debt relief service requests or requires the customer to place funds in an account at an insured financial institution, that the customer owns the funds held in the account, the customer may withdraw from the debt relief service at any time without penalty, and, if the customer withdraws, the customer must receive all funds in the account, other than funds earned by the debt relief service in compliance with § 310.4(a)(5)(i)(A) through (C).

## 3. Misrepresentations

Misrepresenting, directly or by implication, in the sale of goods or services any of the following material information:

3.1. The total costs to purchase, receive, or use, and the quantity of, any goods or services that are the subject of a sales offer;

3.2. Any material restriction, limitation, or condition to purchase, receive, or use goods or services that are the subject of a sales offer;

3.3. Any material aspect of the performance, efficacy, nature, or central characteristics of goods or services that are the subject of a sales offer;

3.4. Any material aspect of the nature or terms of the seller's refund, cancellation, exchange, or repurchase policies;

3.5. Any material aspect of a prize promotion including, but not limited to, the odds of being able to receive a prize, the nature or value of a prize, or that a purchase or payment is required to win a prize or to participate in a prize promotion;

3.6. Any material aspect of an investment opportunity including, but not limited to, risk, liquidity, earnings potential, or profitability;

3.7. A seller's or telemarketer's affiliation with, or endorsement or sponsorship by, any person or government entity;

3.8. That any customer needs offered goods or services to provide protections a customer already has pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1643;

3.9. Any material aspect of a negative option feature including, but not limited to, the fact that the customer's account will be charged unless the customer takes an affirmative action to avoid the charge(s), the date(s) the charge(s) will be submitted for payment, and the specific steps the customer must take to avoid the charge(s); or

3.10. Any material aspect of any debt relief service, including, but not limited to, the amount of money or the percentage of the debt amount that a customer may save by using such service; the amount of time necessary to achieve the represented results; the amount of money or the percentage of each outstanding debt that the customer must accumulate before the provider of the debt relief service will initiate attempts with the customer's creditors or debt collectors or make a bona fide offer to negotiate, settle, or modify the terms of the customer's debt; the effect of the service on a customer's creditworthiness; the effect of the service on collection efforts of the customer's creditors or debt collectors; the percentage or number of customers who attain the represented results; and whether a debt relief service is offered or provided by a non-profit entity.

## 4. Definitions

From 16 CFR 310.2.

4.1. Cardholder means a person to whom a credit card is issued or who is authorized to use a credit card on behalf of or in addition to the person to whom the credit card is issued.

4.2. Credit means the right granted by a creditor to a debtor to defer payment of debt or to incur debt and defer its payment.

4.3. Credit card means any card, plate, coupon book, or other credit device existing for the purpose of obtaining money, property, labor, or services on credit.

4.4. Customer means any person who is or may be required to pay for goods or services offered through telemarketing.

4.5. Debt relief service means any program or service represented, directly or by implication, to renegotiate, settle, or in any way alter the terms of payment or other terms of the debt between a person and one or more unsecured creditors or debt collectors, including, but not limited to, a reduction in the balance, interest rate, or fees owed by a person to an unsecured creditor or debt collector.

4.6. Investment opportunity means anything, tangible or intangible, that is offered, offered for sale, sold, or traded based wholly or in part on representations, either express or implied, about past, present, or future income, profit, or appreciation.

4.7. Material means likely to affect a person's choice of, or conduct regarding, goods or services or a charitable contribution.

4.8. Negative option feature means, in an offer or agreement to sell or provide any goods or services, a provision under which the customer's silence or failure to take an affirmative action to reject goods or services or to cancel the agreement is interpreted by the seller as acceptance of the offer.

4.9. Person means any individual, group, unincorporated association, limited or general partnership, corporation, or other business entity.

4.10. Prize means anything offered, or purportedly offered, and given, or purportedly given, to a person by chance. For purposes of this definition, chance exists if a person is guaranteed to receive an item and, at the time of the offer or purported offer, the telemarketer does not identify the specific item that the person will receive.

4.11. Prize promotion means: (1) A sweepstakes or other game of chance; or (2) An oral or written express or implied representation that a person has won, has been selected to receive, or may be eligible to receive a prize or purported prize.

4.12. Seller means any person who, in connection with a telemarketing transaction, provides, offers to provide, or arranges for others to provide goods or services to the customer in exchange for consideration.

4.13. Telemarketer means any person who, in connection with telemarketing, initiates or receives telephone calls to or from a customer or donor.

4.14. Telemarketing means a plan, program, or campaign which is conducted to induce the purchase of goods or services or a charitable contribution, by use of one or more telephones and which involves more than one interstate telephone call. The term does not include the solicitation of sales through the mailing of a catalog which: contains a written description or illustration of the goods or services offered for sale; includes the business address of the seller; includes multiple pages of written material or illustrations; and has been issued not less frequently than once a year, when the person making the solicitation does not solicit customers by telephone but only receives calls initiated by customers in response to the catalog and during those calls takes orders only without further solicitation. For purposes of the previous sentence, the term “further solicitation” does not include providing the customer with information about, or attempting to sell, any other item included in the same catalog which prompted the customer's call or in a substantially similar catalog.

**Coverage and parties.** An opening line saying the actor "is a telemarketer subject to the Telemarketing Sales Rule" settles several facts:
- induces_purchase_by_telephone, more_than_one_interstate_call, actor_is_seller_or_telemarketer and counterparty_is_customer are yes.
- solicited_through_mailed_catalog is no, unless a catalog is described.

**Consent.** customer_consented_to_pay is yes when the record says the customer bought, agreed, joined, was "sold" or "convinced," or is on the seller's plan. It is no only if the record says the customer declined or paid nothing, as in a free trial that ends unless the customer later opts in.

**Silence.** These records are short and state the defect they raise. Read silence as follows:
- A topic never mentioned (prize, negative option, debt relief, investment, card protection, refund policy) is absent. Its trigger fact is no.
- A misrepresentation fact is no unless the record recounts a statement or description at odds with the truth.
- A required disclosure the record does not call missing, late or vague is yes.
- Fill every fact. Do not leave triggers unknown.

**Disclosure quality.**
- A disclosure is no if the record says it was omitted, given only after the sale, or given in vague terms ("a handful," "a very reasonable price," "a few months or so").
- Concrete terms ("4 brooms for $10," "within 90 days," "exchanges but not refunds") are yes.

**Price.**
- A stated price with an undisclosed extra charge needed to buy, receive or use the goods means total_cost_disclosed is no. Examples are shipping, fees and required parts.
- Quoting a price as if it were complete also misrepresents total cost by implication.
- Stating before consent that an item or fee is excluded from the price discloses the cost truthfully.

**Restrictions and nature.**
- A condition limiting when or how the goods can be used is a material restriction.
- Omitted trivia that does not limit use or change what is sold is neither a material restriction nor a misrepresentation. Examples are origin and the domestic share of goods.
- A description the customer would naturally read as something other than what is delivered misrepresents nature by implication.

**Negative option.**
- Automatic renewal or charges "until cancelled" is a negative option. "Automatically renews monthly after the trial" discloses the charge dates.
- An undisclosed cost of cancelling means negative_option_other_terms_disclosed is no.
- A cancellation method the record states, however burdensome, means negative_option_avoid_steps_disclosed is yes.
